_comment: Learn step by step (/step-by-step): the curated beginner path. Tasks reference reviewed items by ref, they never copy text — see src/lib/einfach-content.js for the ref formats and docs/easy-mode-tier1-v1.md for how to add a unit. Check with: pnpm check:einfach. Portuguese version (beginner-path run, 2026-11-14): European Portuguese, A1, A2 and B1, 35 units in the order of the Portuguese grammar slots. Every task points at a pt-PT grammar item (gram:) or an akkusativ.json item; no task uses the lexicon (wort/artikel via lex:) or redemittel, because those sources are still Spanish until vocab-a1…b1 and speaking: add those tasks back then, one per unit where a word card fits. No task points at an item with ptBR.skip. Hints and whys are English. Postcards are places in Portugal, written here (source: neu) until Edgar has checked them.

units.title: Introduce yourself
claims: You say hello and say your name.
You use eu, tu, o senhor and vocês.

postcard.fact: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal and its biggest city. It lies on the river Tejo, close to the Atlantic.

units.title: Show someone your home
claims: You talk about the things in your home.
You choose o, a, um or uma.

postcard.fact: In Costa Nova, near Aveiro, the houses are painted in bright stripes. They were once fishermen's huts.

tasks.hint: Look at the last letter: -o is often o, -a is often a.
Look at the last letter: -o is often o, -a is often a.
Chaves is more than one thing. Look at the -s.
Cadeira ends in -a. Is it one or more?
A new thing, not yet known: not o or a.
You both know which toilet: the one in this place.

units.title: Say who and where you are
claims: You say who you are with ser.
You say where you are with estar.

postcard.fact: Braga is one of the oldest cities in Portugal. The Romans called it Bracara Augusta.

units.title: Describe your flat
claims: You say what things are like.
You match words: os apartamentos caros.

postcard.fact: Guarda is the highest city in Portugal, at about 1,000 metres. It can be cold even in spring.

units.title: Go shopping
claims: You understand numbers and prices.
You say how much something costs.

postcard.fact: Loulé has a famous market hall in the Algarve. Locals buy fruit, fish and cheese there.

units.title: Get to know someone
claims: You ask and answer yes/no questions.
You ask: Onde? Quando? Quem? Quantos?

postcard.fact: Viseu is a city in the centre of Portugal, in the Dão wine region.

units.title: Talk about your day
claims: You say what you do every day.
You use -ar, -er and -ir verbs.

postcard.fact: Setúbal lies on the river Sado. Dolphins live in the river mouth, and the Arrábida hills are right behind the city.

units.title: At the health centre
claims: You say: tenho, vou and estou.
You say your age with ter.

postcard.fact: The name means “the Queen's hot springs”. People have come here for the thermal water since the 15th century.

units.title: In a café
claims: You order: peço, queria.
You say you did not hear: não ouço bem.

postcard.fact: Belém is a district of Lisbon. A bakery there has sold pastéis de nata since 1837.

units.title: Find your way
claims: You ask: Onde fica…? Há…?
You choose há, está or estão.

postcard.fact: Ponte de Lima is one of the oldest towns in Portugal. It has a long bridge over the river Lima with Roman origins.

units.title: Talk about your family
claims: You talk about your family.
You say o meu, a minha, o nosso.

postcard.fact: The rooster of Barcelos is a symbol of Portugal. Families buy the painted figure as a souvenir.

units.title: Say what you like
claims: You say what you like.
You point at things: este, esta, estes.

postcard.fact: Nazaré is a fishing town. In winter its giant waves attract surfers from all over the world.

units.title: Make an appointment
claims: You say the time: são dez horas.
You say when: na terça, às dez.

postcard.fact: Fátima is a place of pilgrimage. Many thousands of people come on 13 May and 13 October.

units.title: Book a Junta appointment
claims: You ask for an appointment at the Junta.
You say where you live.

postcard.fact: Funchal is the capital of Madeira. Madeira is an island in the Atlantic that belongs to Portugal.

units.title: Say why
claims: You join ideas with e, ou and mas.
You give a reason with porque.

postcard.fact: Ponta Delgada is the largest city of the Azores. It lies on the island of São Miguel.

units.title: Talk about your morning
claims: You talk about your daily routine.
You say: levanto-me, deitas-te, lava-se.

postcard.fact: Near Lagos in the Algarve, the cliffs of Ponta da Piedade rise out of the sea. You can visit them by small boat.

tasks.hint: Look at the word eu.
tasks.why: Levantar-se with eu: levanto-me.

tasks.hint: Deitas: who is it? The -as ending tells you.
tasks.why: The ending -as belongs to tu: tu deitas-te. After a question word the pronoun goes before the verb: te deitas.

tasks.hint: A minha irmã e eu: who is that together?
tasks.why: A minha irmã e eu = nós: lavamo-nos.

tasks.hint: Who gets dressed here? The children, not me.
tasks.why: The action goes to another person, so there is no -me.

tasks.hint: Eu must get up. The pronoun goes on the end.
tasks.why: After tenho de, the pronoun joins the infinitive: levantar-me.
In Portugal the pronoun comes after the verb, with a hyphen: levanto-me.

units.title: Plan your week
claims: You say what you are going to do.
You use ir + infinitive: vou ligar.

postcard.fact: Tavira lies on the river Gilão in the eastern Algarve. A boat takes you to its beach on an island.

tasks.hint: Look at the word eu.
tasks.why: Ir with eu: vou. Vou ligar.

tasks.hint: Look at the word tu.
tasks.why: Ir with tu: vais. O que é que vais fazer?

tasks.hint: After vou, the verb does not change.
tasks.why: After vou comes the infinitive: vou mudar.

tasks.hint: Sai is one person. Keep that person.
tasks.why: Sai → vai sair. The second verb is the infinitive.
Do not add a: vou ligar.

units.title: Say what you are doing
claims: You say what you are doing now.
You choose: every day or right now.

postcard.fact: Peniche is a fishing port. Boats leave from here for the Berlengas islands.

tasks.hint: Look at the word eu. It is happening now.
tasks.why: Happening now: estar a + infinitive. Estou a cozinhar.

tasks.hint: Omar = ele. It is happening now.
tasks.why: Estar with ele: está a falar.

tasks.hint: Between estar and the verb you need a small word.
tasks.why: Estar a + infinitive: estou a falar.

tasks.hint: The verb after estar never changes.
tasks.why: Estar a + infinitive: estou a comer.

tasks.hint: Agora mesmo means right now.
tasks.why: Right now: estar a + infinitive, never ser.

tasks.hint: Todos os dias: is it happening now?
tasks.why: Every day: use the present, not estar a. In Portugal the pronoun comes after the verb.
Está a esperar: estar and a + infinitive stay together.

units.title: Say what you did today
claims: You say what is done and not done yet.
You use já and ainda não.

postcard.fact: Ericeira is a World Surfing Reserve, the first one in Europe.

tasks.hint: Look at the word eu. Ontem is finished.
tasks.why: Falar, eu, past: falei.

tasks.hint: A Ana is one person, not you. Ontem is finished.
tasks.why: Falar and chegar with ele or ela, past: -ou. Chegou.

tasks.hint: Keep the g hard before -e: gu.
tasks.why: Chegar → cheguei, so the g keeps its sound.

tasks.hint: Keep the g hard before -e: gu.
tasks.why: Pagar → paguei, so the g keeps its sound.

tasks.hint: The person has paid. Is it done?
tasks.why: Already done: já paguei.

tasks.hint: The postman has not come. Maybe he comes later.
tasks.why: Not yet: ainda não.
Ainda não + the verb in the perfeito: ainda não comi.

units.title: Talk about last weekend
claims: You say what you did at the weekend.
You use ontem and the pretérito perfeito: fui, tive, fiz.

postcard.fact: Peso da Régua is in the Douro valley, where port wine grapes grow on steep terraces.

tasks.hint: Ontem means yesterday.
tasks.why: Ontem is the past: foi. Vai is the present.

tasks.hint: Todos os dias, and the person is eu.
tasks.why: Every day, eu: faço. Fiz is the past.

tasks.hint: Ontem à noite means last night.
tasks.why: Last night is the past, and ele: veio.

tasks.hint: Antes … todos os dias: a habit.
tasks.why: A habit in the past: imperfeito. Antes ia ao banco.

tasks.hint: Quando era criança: a description.
tasks.why: A description in the past: fazia.
Fazer is irregular: fizeste. O que fizeste?

units.title: Say how life was
claims: You say how life used to be.
You use antes: vivia, era, ia.

postcard.fact: Mértola on the river Guadiana has Roman and Islamic history. The old town is a museum in itself.

tasks.hint: Antes: how things were, for a long time.
tasks.why: How things used to be: imperfeito. Antes vivia.

tasks.hint: What was she like, as a person?
tasks.why: What someone was like: ser in the imperfeito. A minha avó era simpática.

tasks.hint: Há in the past has one form only.
tasks.why: Há in the imperfeito is always havia, even with lojas.

tasks.hint: Antes … agora: then and now.
tasks.why: Antes: trabalhava. Agora: trabalho.

tasks.hint: Ontem, at nine o'clock: one finished event.
tasks.why: One finished event: pretérito perfeito. Ontem fui.
Antes usually goes first. Viver with eu: vivia.
Há in the past: havia.

units.title: Don't repeat the word
claims: You replace a person or thing: vejo-o.
You use me, o, a, os, as.

postcard.fact: Elvas is a fortified town near the Spanish border. Its walls and forts are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

tasks.hint: Tomás is one man.
Amina is one woman.
Os meus pais: more than one person.
After the infinitive ver the r drops. What does o become?
Levam ends in -m. What happens to the pronoun after it?
Where does the pronoun go after estar a?

units.title: Give things to people
claims: You say who gets something: dou-lhe.
You use me, te, lhe, nos, lhes.

postcard.fact: The monastery of Alcobaça is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It holds the tombs of King Pedro and Inês de Castro.

tasks.hint: Who gets the prescription? A mim.
tasks.why: A mim goes with me: dá-me uma receita.

tasks.hint: Ana gets the email. One person.
tasks.why: The person who gets something: lhe, for a woman too.

tasks.hint: Your parents get the money. More than one.
tasks.why: More than one person who gets something: lhes.

tasks.hint: Is there a o or a after the gap?
tasks.why: No o or a here, so: dou-lhe as chaves.

tasks.hint: The key is already named: a chave.
tasks.why: Lhe + a join: lha. Dou-lha.

tasks.hint: Two pronouns. They join into one word.
tasks.why: Lhe + o join: lho. Dou-lho.
In Portugal the pronoun joins the verb: explicam-nos.

units.title: Say what you have to do
claims: You say tenho de, é preciso and posso.
You choose saber or poder.

postcard.fact: The monastery of Batalha is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It took more than a hundred years to build.

tasks.hint: It is about me, this Saturday.
tasks.why: One person must: ter de. Tenho de trabalhar.

tasks.hint: This is a rule for everyone.
tasks.why: Anyone must: é preciso + infinitive.

tasks.hint: O meu marido e eu: two people you can name.
tasks.why: These two people must: temos de.

tasks.hint: Nunca aprendi: never learned.
tasks.why: A skill you have learned: saber. Não sei nadar.

tasks.hint: You can swim, but your arm hurts today.
tasks.why: Possible right now: poder. Hoje não posso.
É preciso + infinitive: a rule for everyone.

units.title: Ask politely
claims: You ask politely: Pode…? Podia…?
You say queria and gostava de.

postcard.fact: The palace and convent of Mafra were built in the 18th century. It is one of the biggest buildings in Portugal.

tasks.hint: You don't know the doctor well.
tasks.why: Someone you don't know well: você or o senhor / a senhora, with pode. Pode repetir?

tasks.hint: A polite way to say what you want.
tasks.why: In a bank or shop, queria is a polite “I'd like”.

tasks.hint: You would like to see the flat.
tasks.why: Gostava de + infinitive = I would like to.

tasks.hint: After podia, the verb stays in the infinitive.
tasks.why: Podia + infinitive: a polite request. Podia trazer-me a conta?

tasks.hint: Importas-te…? means “do you mind?”.
tasks.why: “Do you mind?” “No, I don't.” So you say no.
Queria + infinitive: a polite way to ask.

units.title: Say no
claims: You say: nada, ninguém, nunca.
You use também não and nenhum.

postcard.fact: Chaves in the north has hot springs and a Roman bridge over the river Tâmega.

tasks.hint: It is about things in the fridge.
tasks.why: No things: nada.

tasks.hint: It is about people in the office.
tasks.why: No people: ninguém.

tasks.hint: It is about how often you go.
tasks.why: No time: nunca.

tasks.hint: Problema is masculine.
tasks.why: Before a masculine noun: nenhum problema.

tasks.hint: Ninguém comes before the verb.
tasks.why: Negative word before the verb: no second não.

tasks.hint: The first person says no. You agree.
tasks.why: After a negative sentence, agree with também não.
Não + verb + ninguém.

units.title: Say where things are
claims: You say where things are.
You use em cima de, debaixo de, ao lado de.

postcard.fact: Portalegre in the Alentejo is known for its hand-woven tapestries.

tasks.hint: It is the opposite of “on top of”.
tasks.why: Under: debaixo de. On top of: em cima de.

tasks.hint: The word lado means side.
tasks.why: Next to: ao lado de.

tasks.hint: We say o banco.
tasks.why: De + o = do.

tasks.hint: We say a cama.
tasks.why: De + a = da: debaixo da cama.

tasks.hint: One thing on each side. There is no de.
tasks.why: Between: entre, with no de. Entre o banco e o café.
The thing, then estão, then the place.

units.title: Tell a story
claims: You tell a story in the past.
You choose perfeito or imperfeito.

postcard.fact: The Pena Palace stands on a hill above Sintra and is painted in bright yellow and red.

tasks.hint: A long time in your life, not one event.
tasks.why: Age and childhood are background: imperfeito. Quando era pequena.

tasks.hint: De repente: suddenly, one moment.
tasks.why: A sudden event: perfeito. Tocou.

tasks.hint: One action was in progress. Another one came.
tasks.why: In progress: cozinhava. The event that came: ligou.

tasks.hint: Moving to Portugal happened once. It is finished.
tasks.why: One finished event in the past: mudei.

tasks.hint: How did Ana feel when she went to bed?
tasks.why: A state, the reason for the event: estava.

tasks.hint: Eu dormia is the scene. What happened then?
tasks.why: The scene: dormia. The event: tocou.
The imperfeito sets the scene. The perfeito brings the event.

units.title: Say what had happened
claims: You say what happened before something else.
You use tinha + participle: tinha saído.

postcard.fact: The historic centre of Guimarães is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

tasks.hint: Look at the word já. What came first?
tasks.why: It began before you arrived: tinha começado.

tasks.hint: When did you leave the keys? Before or after?
tasks.why: First you left the keys, then you could not get in: tinha deixado.

tasks.hint: First the exam, then the happy Omar.
tasks.why: The exam came first: tinha passado.

tasks.hint: Eu is the person. Does the participle change?
tasks.why: The participle ends in -o and never changes: tinha estado.

tasks.hint: Escrever has an irregular participle.
tasks.why: Escrever → escrito: tinha escrito.
Tinha + participle stay together: já tinha saído.

units.title: Talk about the future
claims: You say what will happen: choverá, teremos.
You make promises: pagarei, ligarei.

postcard.fact: A Roman temple still stands in the middle of the old town of Évora.

tasks.hint: Amanhã is tomorrow: a forecast.
tasks.why: Tomorrow: futuro simples. Infinitive + -á: choverá.

tasks.hint: A promise from eu, about tomorrow.
tasks.why: Eu in the futuro: -ei after the infinitive. Pagarei.

tasks.hint: Next month. Vir has a short stem in the future.
tasks.why: Vir → virá: a short, irregular form.

tasks.hint: Next year, with nós.
tasks.why: Ter → teremos: the whole infinitive + -emos.

tasks.hint: There will be a meeting. What is há in the future?
tasks.why: Há in the futuro: haverá.
Volto daqui a uma hora: daqui a = in, from now.

units.title: Sort out your flat
claims: You ask politely: gostaria de, poderia…?
You give advice: eu, no teu lugar, iria.

postcard.fact: Óbidos is a small town inside medieval walls, and you can walk along the top of them.

tasks.hint: It is a polite wish now, not the past.
tasks.why: A polite wish about now: Gostaria de marcar uma consulta.

tasks.hint: You are asking politely, with nós.
tasks.why: Gostaríamos de = we would like to; gostamos de = we like.

tasks.hint: You ask a friend, using tu.
tasks.why: The tu form ends in -s: Poderias.

tasks.hint: Eu, no teu lugar: if I were you.
tasks.why: No teu lugar + conditional: iria ao médico.

tasks.hint: Advice for now, not a past action.
tasks.why: No teu lugar + conditional: não assinaria.
Gostaria de + infinitive: a polite wish.

units.title: Tell people what to do
claims: You tell someone what to do: assine aqui.
You tell people what not to do: não fales.

postcard.fact: The Convent of Christ in Tomar was once a stronghold of the Knights Templar.

tasks.hint: You speak to your mother, using tu.
tasks.why: Tu, -ar verb: apaga.

tasks.hint: You speak to a senhora, formally.
tasks.why: A senhora, -ar verb: the ending changes to -e. Assine.

tasks.hint: A formal instruction to o senhor.
tasks.why: Formal: the subjunctive form, traga.

tasks.hint: A negative command with tu.
tasks.why: Não + subjunctive: não chegues.

tasks.hint: A negative command to o senhor.
tasks.why: Não + subjunctive, formal: não fume.

tasks.hint: A positive command with tu. Where does me go?
tasks.why: Positive command: the pronoun follows the verb, with a hyphen.
Negative command: the pronoun goes before the verb.

units.title: Talk about a problem
claims: You say what you want others to do: quero que.
You say how you feel: incomoda-me que.

postcard.fact: Coimbra has one of the oldest universities in Europe, founded in 1290.

tasks.hint: After quero que you need the subjunctive.
tasks.why: Quero que + subjunctive: me ajudes.

tasks.hint: After preciso que you need the subjunctive.
tasks.why: Preciso que + subjunctive: -ar verbs change to -e. Assine.

tasks.hint: A feeling comes first: incomoda-me que.
tasks.why: After a feeling, use the subjunctive: ponha.

tasks.hint: A feeling comes first: tenho pena que.
tasks.why: Tenho pena que + subjunctive: possas.

tasks.hint: Acho que: you give an opinion.
tasks.why: Acho que + indicative: está.

tasks.hint: Espero que: it is a hope, not a fact.
tasks.why: Espero que + subjunctive: esteja.
Incomoda-me que + subjunctive: chegues.

units.title: Describe people and places
claims: You describe people and things more exactly.
You use que, onde and o que.

postcard.fact: Porto lies on the Douro river, and port wine is named after the city.

tasks.hint: It is about a person: a rapariga.
tasks.why: A person, subject of trabalha: que.

tasks.hint: Something happened in this place.
tasks.why: I was born in the village: onde.

tasks.hint: There is no noun before the gap.
tasks.why: No noun: o que = what, the thing that.

tasks.hint: The office itself does the action: fica, fecha.
tasks.why: The place is the subject: que.

tasks.hint: You live in that neighbourhood.
tasks.why: Something happens in the place: onde vivemos.
No noun: o que. O que quero é…

units.title: Ask for information
claims: You ask: Pode dizer-me…? Sabes quando…?
You report what people say and ask.

postcard.fact: Faro is the capital of the Algarve, and its lagoon, the Ria Formosa, is a nature park.

tasks.hint: The direct question is yes/no: Tenho o cartão?
tasks.why: A yes/no question: se.

tasks.hint: You mean: where?
tasks.why: The question word for a place: onde.

tasks.hint: You mean: what?
tasks.why: A question word for things: o que.

tasks.hint: The direct question is: Preciso de marcação?
tasks.why: A yes/no question: se.

tasks.hint: Is onde moro a statement or a question?
tasks.why: Onde moro is a question: pergunta-me.
Pode dizer-me + the question word + the verb.
